newsitem.title: USA: Georgia leading indicators rise for September.
newsitem.headline: Georgia leading indicators rise for September.

text.p: The Georgia index of leading economic indicators rose in September for the third consecutive month, a signal that the state's economy remains sound, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said in his monthly report Friday.
The index of leading indicators, designed to predict economic conditions three-to-six months ahead, rose by 0.99 points to 144.39 on a 1988 benchmark of 100.
The index of coincident indicators, designed to measure current economic conditions, continued to fall from the high reached during this year's Olympic Games in Atlanta.
That index dropped 1.07 points in September to 143.77 on a base of 1987 equal to 100. It peaked at 147.2 during the games in July.
The leading indicators had shown losses in three of the first six months of the year, but have since risen steadily.
"The trend appears to bode well for the economy during the upcoming holiday season," Poythress said.

September's rise in leading indicators was fueled by increases in motor vehicle sales, manufacturing activity and new corporate charters. On the down side, initial unemployment claims rose slightly and demand for new residential building permits was down.

The state reported 42,014 titles were issued for new motor vehicles in Septmeber, up by 271 from August. Applications for new corporate charters rose by 231 to 2,800. The average length of the manufacturing workweek rose to 42.6 hours in Sepember from 42.4 in August.
Initial jobless claims rose to 29,584 in September, an increase of 1.55 percent from August.
The number of new residential building permits dipped to 6,600 in September from 6,778 in August.

Revenues continued to rise sharply. Total revenues rose to $914.8 million in September, an increase of 15.28 percent over September of last year. Sales tax revenues rose to $360 million, up 15.68 percent over last September.
Nonfarm employment declined to 3.55 million in September, down by 6,000 from August but still up by 101,000 or 2.93 percent from a year ago.
Poythress said the workforce was expected to increase during the rest of the year. Georgia's September unemployment rate was unchanged from August at 4.4 percent.
